claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own measurement. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing field, and the trace records 25.4 km against a booked optimal of 19.6 km — an excess of 5.8 km, or 29.59% of optimal. Both gates pass: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute, so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED. I rely on the trace figure, not trip_record.actual_distance_km, which POL-RD-01 forbids citing for the threshold test.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (fare_breakdown.fare_model = UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 24.50), so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run. I do not ask for a distance-or-time refund; the rider is not seeking a remedy the policy does not provide. What POL-RD-11(a) gives her is the whole of the amount by which charged_total (39.00) exceeds the quote plus any properly chargeable pass-through: the ledger's own derived figure is charged_over_quote = 14.50, and 14.50 is refundable in full.

Neither charged gantry lies on the optimal route: both ECP lines carry on_optimal_route = false, optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00, and the optimal_route_source confirms the optimal corridor (PIE to Kallang then Nicoll Hwy) carries no ERP at all. The SGD 6.00 of ERP is therefore not a pass-through properly chargeable to a rider carried off the optimal corridor with no rider instruction, and POL-RD-09 corrects it. It must NOT be added on top of the POL-RD-11(a) figure, because POL-RD-09(1) forbids double counting and the 14.50 over-quote already comprehends the 6.00 of ERP: refund 14.50, not 20.50. Honest note: each gantry is matched to a trace fix at 0 m distance, so I do not allege a phantom line under POL-RD-09(4) — the money claim rests on POL-RD-11(a) and POL-RD-09 pass-through correction, not on billing integrity.

The driver's 'she agreed to take ECP' defence has no artifact behind it. The trip's chat log contains zero messages (message_count 0, messages empty, truncated false), so there is no rider instruction, no timestamp placing it before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and no waypoint_hint against which POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test could be run. POL-RD-04 says in terms that where no road is named and waypoint_hint is null the corroboration test is undecidable, the clause is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. POL-RD-08 puts the burden on the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; a bare assertion in a counterparty_statement does not discharge it, and his statement that the fare should have updated 'is not my problem' is not a defence the policy recognises.

The congestion defence fails the same way. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached that segment. The only advisory in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00501-01, is MISSING: payload null, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING), weight_multiplier 0.0. There is nothing to name PIE and nothing to date it, and the absence is itself citable. Disclosure: that artifact is impaired at weight 0.0 and I cite it only for its absence; 'I checked the map' is a general assertion of bad traffic, which under POL-RD-08 carries no weight without a traffic_advisory ID.

The rider's POL-RD-08 burden is discharged, and the artifacts describe the same trip: trip_id TRP-00501 runs through trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and the trace opens at 14:11:40, exactly trip_record.started_at. The trace is unimpaired on the POL-RD-07 test — 163 fixes at a 10 second cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, gaps empty and max_gap_sec 0.0 — so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires, no stretch has to be measured as a straight line between bounding fixes, and the excess stands on the trace alone. The artifact is also admissibility-COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so nothing in POL-GEN-02 discounts it.

Independently of the trace, the fare ledger's charged gantry set places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use: ECP (Fort Rd towards City) charged at 14:28:30 and ECP (Rochor towards City) at 14:33:20, each matched to a trace fix at 0 m. That is precisely the species of independent corroboration POL-RD-07(ii) names — the set of erp_gantries actually charged in the fare_breakdown placing the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use — and it carries the excess even if the trace were impugned.

The extra-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 is not in play: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the 4-or-more trigger never fires and the trace alone carries the excess without any further source. Nothing else on either profile is used in this brief: under POL-GEN-01 every other field on the rider and driver profiles — lifetime counters, ratings, prior flags — is context only and cannot ground a finding here.

The SGD 2.90 customer-service offer has no basis in the arithmetic. The only figures the policy produces on this record are quoted 24.50 and charged 39.00, a difference of 14.50 — far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis — so the outcome for the filing party is PARTIAL_REFUND of the 39.00 contested, not a goodwill credit, and the rider should be left paying the quote of 24.50 and nothing at all for the detour. That is a ruling that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge, which is what a rider win comes down to.

claims.text: The governing measurement is the trace, and on this trip it clears the establishment gate but stops well short of materiality. EV-GPS-00501 is complete and unimpaired — 163 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so none of the POL-RD-07(a)-(c) impairment conditions is met — and it records trace_distance_km 25.4 against an optimal of 19.6 km, an excess of 5.8 km and 29.6%. POL-RD-01 makes that deviation ESTABLISHED (over 20% and over 0.8 km) but not MATERIAL, because it is under both the 50% and the 8.0 km lines; the escalated consequences POL-RD-06 attaches to materiality therefore never arise. The driver does not dispute the establishment finding; he disputes what follows from it.

No repeat-deviation pattern exists against this driver, and none may be built from his record. POL-RD-06's consultation was not even triggered, because the deviation is not material; and if it is run anyway it returns nothing: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither the '3 or more flags' limb nor the '0.05 ratio with at least 40 trips' limb is satisfied. There is accordingly no balance-tilt toward the rider, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names and may not be substituted for it.

The fare model closes the refund the rider is really asking for. fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 24.50, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines, and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the 5.8 km excess is. The SGD 14.50 the claim rests on is nothing more than charged_total 39.00 less quoted_fare_sgd 24.50 — a gap between two totals, not a loss the rider bore on distance or time. On this fare model the extra kilometres are the driver's loss, and he has already absorbed them.

Neither ERP line is a phantom charge, so no billing-integrity refund is due under POL-RD-09(4). The trace carries a fix 0.0 m from the ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry — fix index 101 at 14:28:30, the exact timestamp at which the first SGD 3.00 was charged — and a fix 0.0 m from the ECP (Rochor towards City) gantry — fix index 130 at 14:33:20, the exact timestamp of the second SGD 3.00. Both are far inside POL-RD-09's 250 m match radius, so both gantries were actually crossed by this vehicle on this trip. There is nothing unmatched here for the rider to have refunded.

Run POL-RD-11(a) as written and the refund is small. The rider's remedy is the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, and POL-RD-11(a) describes that basket as 'ERP and tolls actually crossed' — not as gantries on the optimal route. POL-RD-09(1)'s on-optimal-route-only treatment is expressly tied to a POL-RD-02 refund, and POL-RD-11 says POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront-quoted trip. Deducting only the two ERP lines actually crossed (SGD 6.00), the refund is 39.00 - (24.50 + 6.00) = SGD 8.50. It is not the SGD 14.50 the claim implies, and it is not the full SGD 39.00 contested.

The basket is in fact wider still, and the refund correspondingly smaller. This trip ORIGINATES at Changi Terminal 3, so under the fare model an off-peak Changi surcharge of SGD 6.00 is properly chargeable on it, and the ledger applied 0.00 of it. POL-RD-11(a) names 'a properly chargeable airport surcharge' in the deduction — properly chargeable, not merely charged — so the basket is 24.50 + 6.00 (ERP actually crossed) + 6.00 (properly chargeable surcharge) = 36.50, and the refund is 39.00 - 36.50 = SGD 2.50. On either reading of the basket the rider's complaint of being overcharged is answered: the charged total does not even reach what the rate card entitled the driver to bill.

The driver does not ask to be exonerated on the strength of any rider instruction, and the record would not let him. The chat log for this trip carries zero messages (message_count 0, truncated false), so no rider instruction is recorded, no waypoint_hint exists and the corroboration POL-RD-04 requires — the vehicle passing within 200 m of a requested waypoint, or travelling a named road — cannot be run. POL-RD-04 itself directs that the clause is then unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses, which is precisely what the driver asks for. Nothing in the record contradicts the driver's contemporaneous account; the money is fixed by POL-RD-11 either way.

The driver likewise claims no closure or traffic-event exoneration, and none is available: the only TRAFFIC_ADVISORY artifact in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00501-01, is MISSING — no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — so no advisory names any road or segment this route traverses. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, discharges nothing, and the driver does not rest on it. He rests instead on POL-RD-11, which operates on the face of the ledger (fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 24.50) and limits the rider's remedy without any finding about the driver's conduct. The detour is conceded at 5.8 km and 29.6%; its consequence is the non-material one.

ruling.explanation:
To both of you — this is what the record shows and what the policy gives.

THE ROUTE. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00501) is complete: 163 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and no gap-measurement or corroboration rule is engaged. It measures 25.4 km driven against the 19.6 km booked optimal route — an excess of 5.8 km, or 29.6%. That is a route deviation ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01 (over both the 20% and the 0.8 km gates), but it is under both materiality lines (50% and 8.0 km), so no repeat-pattern review is required and I make no adverse conduct finding. Both advocates agree on this, and so do I.

THE MONEY. This trip was quoted upfront: fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and the quote is SGD 24.50, against SGD 39.00 charged. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run, so no distance-or-time refund is owed however large the 5.8 km excess is. The rider is right that the detour's extra kilometres are not hers to pay; the driver is right that on this fare model they are his loss and cannot be recovered from her.

What remains is the pass-through basket, and POL-RD-11(a) refunds the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09:
• quoted fare: 24.50
• properly chargeable airport surcharge: 6.00 — the trip originates at Changi Terminal 3, so the surcharge applies, and the trip ran on a Thursday at 14:05, off-peak, so the rate is SGD 6.00.
• ERP properly chargeable: 0.00 — both SGD 3.00 ECP lines sit off the optimal route (on_optimal_route false; the optimal corridor PIE–Kallang–Nicoll Hwy carries no ERP). The trace passes each gantry at 0 m, so they are real crossings and not phantom charges, but POL-RD-11(b) requires off-route gantry charges to be corrected back to the rider.
Correct bill: 24.50 + 6.00 = 30.50. Refund: 39.00 − 30.50 = SGD 8.50.

On the figures argued: the rider's SGD 14.50 wrongly refunds the airport surcharge she properly owes on a Changi-originating trip; the driver's SGD 2.50 wrongly leaves her paying SGD 6.00 of ERP for a detour she did not ask for. The driver's alternative figure of SGD 8.50 reaches the right amount, though by deducting the two ERP lines rather than the surcharge.

THE TWO DEFENCES. Neither exculpates the driver, and neither forces an escalation:
• Rider-requested detour (POL-RD-04). The trip's chat log (EV-CHAT-00501) is empty — 0 messages — so there is no recorded rider instruction and no waypoint_hint. POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. The rider's own recollection that she said 'okay' does not substitute for the recorded instruction the clause requires, so the detour is not treated as rider-caused and the off-route ERP stays refundable.
• Road closure or bad traffic (POL-RD-03). The only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00501-01, is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSSING_ARTIFACT, no payload. It can carry no fact; I cite it only for its absence. 'PIE was crawling' is a general assertion of bad traffic, which under POL-RD-08 carries no weight without a traffic advisory, and it discharges nothing.

PROFILES. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 250 completed trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral fires. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no extra corroboration beyond the trace is required. Every other profile field — ratings, lifetime counters, prior_deviation_flags — is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used. No billing-integrity referral arises either: both gantries were crossed and no surcharge was wrongly applied.

The customer-service offer of SGD 2.90 is not the measure of this dispute; the arithmetic above is.

OUTCOME: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.50 to the rider, leaving SGD 30.50 payable — the booked quote plus the airport surcharge. No driver compensation, no referral, and no escalation.

Both of you: this was an upfront-quoted trip (fare_breakdown.fare_model = UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 24.50), so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and POL-RD-11 governs. The deviation itself is established on the platform's own trace: gps_trace.trace_distance_km 25.4 km against the booked optimal 19.6 km — an excess of 5.8 km, 29.6% — above the POL-RD-01 gate (over 0.8 km and over 20%) but below both materiality lines (50% and 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 driver-profile uplift and no conduct referral arise (and the profile check returns nothing anyway: deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 250; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01). The trace is complete and unimpaired (163 fixes, 10 s cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-07 changes nothing and the excess stands on the trace, independently corroborated by the charged ECP gantry set.

The rider's remedy under POL-RD-11(a) is the amount by which charged_total 39.00 exceeds quoted_fare_sgd 24.50 plus only those pass-through lines properly chargeable to her under POL-RD-09. The optimal corridor carries no ERP (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00), and the 6.00 of ECP gantry charges is off-route (both lines on_optimal_route = false). The detour was neither exonerated under POL-RD-03 — there is no traffic advisory: EV-ADVIS-00501-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its absence is citable but carries no fact, drags no confidence and forces no escalation because no exculpatory clause is invoked against it — nor rider-requested under POL-RD-04, because the chat log for this trip holds 0 messages, so there is no instruction, no timestamp and no waypoint_hint; the corroboration test could not be run and, as POL-RD-04 itself directs, the case is decided on the remaining clauses. The 6.00 of off-route ERP therefore is not properly chargeable to the rider and comes back to her; it is NOT added on top of the over-quote figure, which already contains it — 14.50, not 20.50.

Refund: charged_total 39.00 − quoted_fare 24.50 = SGD 14.50, leaving the rider paying the quote of 24.50 and nothing for the detour or its ERP. I have not accepted the driver's narrower baskets. The 8.50 basket would leave the rider bearing the 6.00 of off-route ERP that POL-RD-09 says a rider who did not cause the detour should not bear. The further deduction of a 6.00 Changi surcharge fails because the ledger's airport_surcharge line is 0.00 — no surcharge was charged, and a charge the platform never levied cannot be conjured into the deduction to shrink the rider's refund (if the platform believes a properly chargeable surcharge went unbilled, that is a matter for its own billing, not for this ruling). The driver likewise claims no closure or traffic-event exoneration, and none is available: the only TRAFFIC_ADVISORY artifact in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00501-01, is MISSING — no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — so no advisory names any road or segment this route traverses. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, discharges nothing, and the driver does not rest on it. He rests instead on POL-RD-11, which operates on the face of the ledger (fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 24.50) and limits the rider's remedy without any finding about the driver's conduct. The detour is conceded at 5.8 km and 29.6%; its consequence is the non-material one.
